summary: Reproduced TeaCache's stale-branch reset behavior, then made request-start reset use the current CFG branch and CFG-parallel topology. Wan skip boundaries now double only for serial CFG, where both branches execute locally. Added regression coverage for serial double reset, serial next-request reset, CFG-parallel negative-rank isolation, noninitial timesteps, and boundary scaling.

tests.what_was_measured: Before the fix, the serial negative timestep-0 call changed cnt from 1 to 0, and a subsequent CFG-parallel negative request retained cnt=50 plus cached tensors and accumulator=7.0. Raw output: reports/j-a18a6c35f2b5/raw/reproduction_before.txt
46 tests and 23 subtests passed, covering TeaCache lifecycle and independent sampling-parameter boundaries. Raw output: reports/j-a18a6c35f2b5/raw/pytest_focused.txt
On AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950, GPU-resident negative cached tensors were cleared and cnt/accumulator reset at CFG-parallel request start. Raw output: reports/j-a18a6c35f2b5/raw/gpu_state_check.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: Single assigned AMD Instinct MI350X (gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-) executed the cache-state reset check with GPU-resident tensors; see reports/j-a18a6c35f2b5/raw/gpu_state_check.txt.

remaining_limitations: No Wan model weights were available, so no full diffusion generation or semantic/image-quality validation was performed.
Only one assigned GPU was available; CFG-parallel rank behavior was tested deterministically through the actual TeaCache implementation, not a live multi-rank workload.
Ruff is not installed in the prepared interpreter or shell environment; git diff --check and Python compilation passed.
